_note: Hand-written market take, refreshed twice a day (~8am and ~8pm UTC) by a separate scheduled research pass. Not touched by scripts/sync.py's automatic hourly sync. This is the site's hero paragraph (first thing under the H1 title), shown under the 'Today's Call' label. Not financial advice.
text: Bitcoin is holding onto its rebound this morning, trading near $81,200, up almost 4% in the past day, right where the site's last update left off. The clearest piece of good news is that the thing we were watching for actually showed up: after two straight days of outflows, spot Bitcoin ETFs flipped back to net inflows on September 17th and 18th, pulling in a combined $590 million or so, which is real money coming in rather than shorts getting squeezed out. On top of that, Bitcoin's daily chart just printed a golden cross, the 50-day average crossing above the 200-day, a setup that's historically tied to the start of bull runs. That said, the signal has a messier track record than people assume, and one analyst who's tracked every past golden cross points out each one has still been followed by a 10 to 15 percent dip before the bigger trend resumed, which from current levels would put a shakeout toward $70,000 to $75,000 well within reach even if the uptrend stays intact. So the setup right now looks genuinely constructive rather than just short-covering noise, but it isn't a straight line, and how price behaves on any pullback will say more about the next few weeks than today's green candle does. Bulls have the better argument at the moment given the flow data, but this is a read on where things stand, not a signal to trade on by itself.
